title: Orchestration Handbook — Q2 Bridge and Escalation Hatches (v0.1)
content:
PURPOSE:
This is a lightweight working handbook to carry the company from now until the end of Q2. Focus: 1) align cross-company priorities (what matters); 2) draft the Q2 OKR scaffold for exec review; 3) provide an explicit escalation ladder and ‘escape hatch’ triggers for the all-team sprint weeks and the company bridge period (weeks where shipping risk increases).

SCOPE / AUDIENCE:
- Audience: execs (brief), managers (tactical), team leads (ops).
- Not a final comms piece — this is a living draft for Company Ops and Execs to iterate before the public all-team note.

QUICK CONTEXT (notes to self):
- We have a tight timeline: product launches in late May; dedicated capacity upsell program rolling in mid‑June; private deployment pilot ramping.
- Known constraints: limited Dedicated GPU pool between 5/15–6/15 (capacity window — see JIRA-2384).
- Primary risk: overlapping rollout of pricing + Dedicated offering causing support surge.

ONE-LINER PRIORITY (for comms):
"Keep the platform stable and predictable while accelerating customer access to Dedicated capacity — prioritize reliability, predictable latency, and clear escalation flows."

PROPOSED Q2 OKR SCAFFOLD (draft — high level):
Objective A: Deliver predictable inference for early enterprise Dedicated customers.
- KR A1: Achieve 99.95% uptime on Dedicated control plane across trial customers (measured monthly).
- KR A2: Validate performance profiles (p99 latency < target on 80% of production traces) for top-3 enterprise workloads.
- KR A3: Complete two on-prem pilot deployments with audit log verification and KMS integration.

Objective B: Reduce per-token unit cost for common web workloads.
- KR B1: Deploy batching + prefix-caching config recommendations to 3 major customers; measure median cost delta >= 18%.
- KR B2: Run quantization A/B on sample workloads and document quality regressions (target: <= 3% noticeable regression for non-chat tasks).
- KR B3: Publish Optimize playbook + automated advisor in Console (beta).

Objective C: Strengthen developer experience and observability for rollouts.
- KR C1: Ship token-level cost traces in Console for top-20 routes.
- KR C2: Integrate rollout canary dashboards and automated rollback policy for two model families.
- KR C3: Reduce mean time to detect (MTTD) regression by 30% via eval-triggered alerts.

NOTES ON KRs: these are intentionally pragmatic; measurement hooks must be defined in product-ops ticket (see linked JIRA-2397).

ALL-TEAM / EXEC UPDATE SLATE (speaker bullets — 8–10 minutes):
- Opening: state the north star (predictable, low-latency inference everywhere).
- Wins: Dedicated beta onboarding, early on‑prem baseline metrics, Console cost traces in private beta.
- Risks: limited Dedicated capacity next 4 weeks; potential support surge during pricing change.
- Ask: teams to prioritize stability work and validate the canary rollback flows by 5/10.
- Closing: what to expect in the next 30 days and where to find the detailed playbook.

ALL-TEAM AGENDA (proposed 60min):
1) Quick mission update (6m) — CEO
2) Reliability + Dedicated status (10m) — Eng + Infra lead
3) Product roadmap highlights (10m) — PM lead
4) Console / Optimize demos (10m) — DevX
5) Escalation & staffing expectations for the bridge weeks (8m) — SRE/People Ops
6) Q&A and channels for follow ups (16m)

ESCALATION LADDER & ESCAPE HATCHES (operational):
- Trigger levels (examples):
  * Level 1 (alerting): p95 latency > SLO for 15m — page oncall, post incident stub on #ops-incidents.
  * Level 2 (service impact): p99 degraded AND error rate increased by >1% — SRE lead + infra exec call within 30m.
  * Level 3 (customer impact / enterprise outage): customer-reported SLA breach or Dedicated pool down — Engage CS leader, exec bridge within 15m, consider traffic routing rollback.

- Escape hatches (pre-approved):
  * Roll back model serving image to last verified tag.
  * Route heavy traffic to hosted model variants (cost increase but lower risk) for up to 72 hours.
  * Enable extra burst capacity from cloud partner (cost-approved via Finance for emergency).

- Ownership matrix (quick):
  * SRE: lead oncall, runbook owner.
  * Infra Eng: capacity/fallbacks.
  * CS/Escalations: customer comms.
  * Product Ops: decision log and canary sign-off.

DECISION LOG (working):
- DRAFT-01 (02/05): approve Hosted fallback for Dedicated capacity shortages as first default. (owner: Marco Lin — action: document routing policy).
- DRAFT-02 (02/07): restrict auto-quantization for enterprise pilots until quality gates implemented. (owner: Priya Kapoor).

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISKS (to resolve before public comms):
- Finance: do we have pre-approved emergency budget for cloud burst > $X/day? (owner: Finance lead).
- Comms: what’s the external messaging if we route enterprise traffic temporarily to hosted? (owner: Growth comms).
- Legal: any contractual constraint with pilot customers on fallback routing? (owner: Legal).

COMMUNICATIONS PLAN (brief):
- Internal: publish final playbook + decision log to Confluence on 2/18; send an executive summary email post-review.
- External (customers): templated notice to pilot customers if a fallback is invoked; CS to run dry-run messages for approval.

MEETING & REVIEW TIMELINE (short):
- 2/10: Product Ops to circulate updated KRs and measurement definitions.
- 2/12: Exec review (15m) of OKRs — sign-off or iterate.
- 2/14: Company Ops publishes the final playbook for the all-team.

NEXT ACTIONS (owners & quick todos):
- Marco: write routing policy doc + JIRA (by 2/7).
- Priya: lock down quantization gating criteria and add to test matrix (by 2/11).
- Ava (owner): assemble final exec slide + speaking notes (by 2/12).
- Ethan: run SRE tabletop for Level 2/3 scenarios (schedule 2/8).

NOTES TO SELF / WORKING THOUGHTS (informal):
- Keep language in the public note short and calming; avoid technical detail that adds friction.
- Consider a one‑pager for sales to explain fallback behavior so they can set expectations with pilot customers.

ATTACHMENTS / REFERENCES (working):
- JIRA-2384 (Dedicated capacity calendar and constraints).
- Confluence: orchestration playbook draft (linked_artifacts above).
- Slack: #ops-incidents and #pilot-cs threads for example comm templates.

If you’re reading this and want edit access: flag in the doc and I’ll add you. This is intentionally concise — we will expand the ‘runbooks’ folder with step-by-step scripts once the KRs land.

-- Ava R. (company-ops)
